name: Retail
title: Store replenishment exception desk
summary: Reconcile shelf observations, inventory records, and delivery plans into manager-approved replenishment actions.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A grocery chain sees apparent stockouts despite positive store inventory. Shelf photographs, point-of-sale activity, damaged-goods records, and backroom counts disagree. Store managers need a short task list that distinguishes a shelf gap from a receiving error or a genuinely unavailable item.
problem: Inventory snapshots can lag sales and waste adjustments. Sending every discrepancy straight to purchasing creates excess stock, while treating shelf-image recognition as certain can dispatch staff to the wrong location or product variant.
whyAgents: Specialists examine shelf evidence, ledger movements, inbound supply, and store task capacity. Their findings feed a deterministic inventory reconciliation and a bounded task proposal; agents do not independently alter counts or purchase stock.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Track useful staff checks and inventory corrections separately from sales. Improved shelf availability is an operational hypothesis to test against comparable stores, not an outcome guaranteed by adding agents.

agents.name: Shelf evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Identify candidate shelf gaps and attach image coordinates and product-match uncertainty.
agents.boundary: Cannot convert an image observation into an inventory adjustment.

agents.name: Inventory reconciler
agents.responsibility: Compare sales, receipts, transfers, and waste events for the affected SKU.
agents.boundary: Cannot post stock corrections or conceal negative balances.

agents.name: Inbound supply analyst
agents.responsibility: Check delivery appointments and order-line status for missing items.
agents.boundary: Cannot create purchase orders or change supplier commitments.

agents.name: Store task planner
agents.responsibility: Propose a backroom check, count, or shelf refill according to staffing and store rules.
agents.boundary: Managers approve assignments and any inventory correction.

systems.name: Point-of-sale and inventory systems
systems.role: Provide item movements with event timestamps and authoritative quantity adjustments.

systems.name: Planogram and product master
systems.role: Resolve shelf positions, pack sizes, substitutions, and product identifiers.

systems.name: Store operations platform
systems.role: Owns staff assignments, task completion evidence, and manager approvals.

flow.title: Register shelf gap
flow.description: Bind the observation to store, shelf, SKU candidates, and capture time; reject ambiguous location metadata.

flow.title: Reconcile movements
flow.description: Read the inventory watermark and all later sales or adjustments before explaining the discrepancy.

flow.title: Inspect alternatives
flow.description: Check backroom locations, substitute package identifiers, and scheduled inbound quantities while preserving uncertainty in product matches.

flow.title: Choose operational check
flow.description: Apply store rules to propose a shelf refill, physical count, receiving investigation, or monitored wait for inbound supply.

flow.title: Review manager task
flow.description: Show supporting evidence and expected staff effort; require explicit review for count adjustments or supplier-order changes.

flow.title: Close evidence loop
flow.description: Record the worker's scan or count, reconcile the ledger through authorized tools, and label the original hypothesis confirmed or rejected.

sequenceDiagram
    participant O as "Case orchestrator"
    participant S as "Point-of-sale and inventory systems"
    participant H as "Accountable reviewer"
O->>S: Read inventory watermark
    S-->>O: Snapshot predates shelf observation

    H-->>O: Confirm SKU and physical count
    O->>S: Refresh movement ledger
    O->>H: Present reconciled refill task
diagrams.caption: Inventory feed lags a sales burst. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: Inventory feed lags a sales burst.
failures.detection: Movement watermark predates the shelf observation beyond the store's configured freshness limit.
failures.recovery: Hold quantity-based recommendations and request a current scan or refreshed ledger snapshot.

failures.scenario: Image matching confuses similar package sizes.
failures.detection: Product confidence and planogram identifier checks disagree.
failures.recovery: Present both candidates and require a barcode scan before creating a SKU-specific task.

controls: Use barcode or governed product identifiers before committing inventory changes.
Exclude shopper and employee identity from shelf-image processing where unnecessary.
Record pack-size conversions explicitly and calculate quantities deterministically.
Require manager approval for adjustments, orders, and substitution-policy changes.
Deduplicate tasks by store, shelf, SKU, and active investigation window.

metrics.name: Shelf-gap validation
metrics.definition: Reported shelf gaps confirmed by staff divided by shelf gaps investigated.

metrics.name: Task preparation latency
metrics.definition: Time from valid observation to manager-ready task, excluding store execution delay.

metrics.name: Inventory freshness
metrics.definition: Age of the latest reconciled movement watermark at recommendation time, reported by store.

metrics.name: Duplicate task rate
metrics.definition: Tasks merged or rejected as duplicate work divided by proposed tasks.

tradeoffs.benefit: Finds discrepancies invisible to either source alone.
tradeoffs.cost: Adds product ambiguity and image-governance work.

tradeoffs.benefit: Fits store accountability and staffing constraints.
tradeoffs.cost: Busy shifts can delay otherwise useful recommendations.

tradeoffs.benefit: Limits cross-store data exposure and latency.
tradeoffs.cost: Central analytics must aggregate outcomes without losing local context.

rollout.acceptance: Managers validate pack conversions, stale inventory handling, and visually similar products using known examples.
One store group compares proposed checks with actual staff findings and verifies image minimization.
Managers enable approved assignments after duplicate-task and late-ledger-update exercises pass.
